preamble: Lowering of the nucleus of a front closing diphthong [ei]/[ɛi] to [ai]. It recurs independently across West Germanic: Middle High German ei became New High German [aɪ], the Dutch ij/ei diphthong is lowered to [ai] in Polder Dutch, and the FACE diphthong of Cockney and similar accents has a nucleus as open as [a].

examples.note: The original MHG diphthongs ei, ou, öu were lowered in Early New High German and fell together with the new diphthongs from î, û, iu.
Among younger speakers in Utrecht, North Holland and South Holland, /ɛi/ is increasingly lowered to [ai]; the change emerged around the 1970s.
Cockney /æj/ corresponds to RP /eɪ/ and is realised as [æj~aj].
